grh_0d7235af837918ce162e.title: Milk Racket Pt1
paragraphs: A series of suspicious highway crashes has been wrecking milk trucks around Rivers End, and the latest collision kills a driver. Witnesses place young Bob Marvin on the truck that caused the fatal wreck, leaving him facing a manslaughter charge even though he says he was not driving and refuses to identify the man who was. Dr. Christian and attorney James Benson Clark discover that Bob's unusually well-paid job with the Farmers' Protective Organization may connect him to a protection racket that has been targeting milk dealers who do not cooperate. Bob is indicted and the case is rushed toward trial. Then a representative of the organization offers Dr. Christian first $20,000 and then $30,000 to leave the state before he can testify. Christian refuses, and the man answers with a direct threat that the doctor will never reach the witness stand, ending the first part with the racket openly moving against him.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on February 27, 1938. It is listed as episode 17 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.66b0cf9e2ff52610|Vaseline (Album Of Hollywood Stars premium)]].

grh_0d2615399bce63f36709.title: Voodoo
paragraphs: Stranded in Haiti, Harry learns that the lost jeweled scepter of national hero Henri Christophe is still secretly guarded by local believers. He pressures his friends Fancy and Greek into revealing enough of the secret to sell the information to wealthy Sam Talkin, putting all of them in danger. A voodoo ceremony ends with Talkin dead and Fancy and Greek marked for sacrifice because the scepter has been betrayed. Harry interrupts the ritual, admits that he was the one who sold the secret, and frees his friends at gunpoint. He then pauses during their escape to steal the scepter himself and later sells it to a collector in Brussels.

The surviving recording runs about 27 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Harry Lime]].
